description:
Independent verification at checked SHA e60986923 confirmed that two functions
named `get_benchmark_class` intentionally return different surfaces:

  benchbox.core.benchmark_registry.get_benchmark_class("tpch")
    -> benchbox.tpch.TPCH
  benchbox.core.benchmark_loader.get_benchmark_class("tpch")
    -> benchbox.core.tpch.benchmark.TPCHBenchmark

The same split was confirmed for `vector_search` and `datavault`. Both
returns are callable benchmark classes, so importing the wrong function can
silently select the public wrapper surface where a core implementation was
expected, or vice versa. Existing tests already alias these functions to keep
them straight, which is evidence that the ambiguity is real.

Independent verification also confirmed the constructor fallback concern in
`benchbox/core/benchmark_loader.py`: a class whose constructor accepts
`parallel` but raises `TypeError` internally is retried without `parallel`,
returning successfully in the mocked harness after constructor calls
`[1, None]`. This means "constructor does not accept `parallel`" and
"constructor accepted `parallel` but had an internal TypeError" are currently
indistinguishable.
